reviews.title: Great game with so much potential
reviews.text: I’m enjoying my first play through and have made notes about what I find needs fixed or adjusted. I hope these critiques are met well and not offensive. This is a great game all in all! Im currently playing as a lesbian, and when I go to make love, the response to skip protection acts as if I’ll get pregnant. Minor thing just something to make more inclusive. A better adjustment to your finances would be great, as I can’t tell what amount I’m agreeing to spend, say for example when I pay for my children’s housing after college. It would be great for my wife or partner to work and add their income in. And the frequency of pay is quite low. Another adjustment would be cool would be seeing your assets. So I can sell my houses. Or cars. Etc. I’d love to keep playing! I’m apprehensive about buying the dlcs until some things are fixed though. I’ll add more if more comes to mind but these are the big ones I’ve noted.

reviews.title: Just downloaded but really enjoying so far!
reviews.text:
I didn’t play the first game so I can’t compare the two, but I’m having a lot of fun playing through my first life. The game has some similarities to Bitlife, but is way more fleshed out in my opinion. The added interactions and dialogue between friends, partners, and family-members makes me actually care about each character way more than I expected. The careers and overall life sim has a decent amount of depth for what’s basically a text-based game (although I think the included art is pretty cute). I like the stats system; it makes it easier to figure out which aspect of my character I want to work on. 
Overall I’d definitely recommend!

I did notice a couple bugs/ issues that dampened some of my enjoyment. I realize this game is pretty new so I’ll leave them below for the devs and hope that they’ll get ironed out in future updates:
1. My character got a part time job over the summer while in college, but her ‘grades’ stat was still punished. The summer season specifically mentioned that my character was getting a break from studying so it was a little annoying that I was punished for working. 
2. There’s either no way to view purchased houses or it’s really hard to find. I clicked on the “buy and sell homes” button, but I only seem to have the option to buy. 
3. I moved one of my character’s friends into her home and then started an affair with her. Even though she knew I was married and that we were having an affair (she literally lived in the same house as my wife), any time I tried to interact with her, I’d get events that acted like *I* was cheating on *her*. It made it impossible to actually play out the messy story I was trying to make lol. 
4. The parenting skill is a little annoying (at least in my first playthrough). I’m trying to interact or take care of my kids and no matter what I do, the interaction goes poorly and my kids are worse off. My character had 3 kids and the one that did the best was the one I interacted with the least. I was trying to improve my parenting skill, but the only way it seems like I can do that is by reading a parenting book which only improves my skill by like. 3-5 points at a time. I eventually stopped trying to improve my character’s relationship with her kids 1-on-1 and just started doing group interactions within the household section of my relationships. 
From a gameplay perspective, I felt like I was being punished for trying to be active in the lives of my characters’ children. I eventually did the video game equivalent of going out for milk and not returning and the kids were *happier*. 
I think it would be beneficial if skills were improved not just by doing the ‘improve skill’ action, but by also engaging in activities associated with the skill. 

I noticed there’s some ‘test skill’ interactions for each skill, but I haven’t really engaged with them much at all because unless you’re writing a book or something that makes money, there doesn’t seem to be much incentive to do so. 
I thought if I did a parenting skill check I could get a boost to the skill if it succeeded, but that didn’t really happen. 
Some kind of change to the skill system would be much appreciated because right now I’m really only raising my character’s skill that relates to her career and nothing else. There doesn’t seem to be much of a reason to if they can only increase by a couple points at a time and any decent outcomes are locked behind a high skill level. 

Despite these issues, I’m still enjoying the game and I’m looking forward to seeing it evolve in the future!

reviews.title: Amazing Game in Development
reviews.text:
Super rich game that is free to play! The developer is also super friendly, receptive to feedback, and fast with implementing bug fixes. The community is also cool too. Overall great game that will only get better!

While the mechanics are similar to BitLife, the vibes of this game are far more cozy. The music is sweet and soothing, and the sound effects remind me of Animal Crossing. You can also restore purchases from Everlife 1 very easily, so you have all of your old expansion packs.

The cute aesthetic combined with the active developer and the charming community make this game perfect for me :)

reviews.title: A life sim with personality
reviews.text:
I’m early in Everlife 2, but it’s made a great first impression. The art is charming, character creation has lots of options, and the little jokes give the writing personality. Being able to continue a family’s story across generations is what I’m most excited to explore.

I really appreciate that it works offline, doesn’t require an account, and has no waiting timers or currencies to buy. It’s also encouraging to see the developer actively answering questions and responding to player feedback. Clearer explanations of starting stats and how traits unlock would make getting started even smoother. There’s a lot of care here, and I’m looking forward to seeing where my character’s life goes!

reviews.title: Iconic
reviews.text:
Everlife 2 is a sequel worthy of it’s name. I played the first game a lot but it often felt repetitive which made the game annoying sometimes. The changes in Everlife 2 attempt to fix that. By allowing your character to have individual relationships, you have the chance to have different lives & stories even if you play as a nice person every life. 

In this game your relationships are much more front and center which I really like. Your family & friends affect your life even if you don’t interact with them proactively. There’s a charm in this game I haven’t felt in this genre in a while. It’s more about living life than making money and doing crazy stuff.

The generations aspect is really well done too! I normally don’t use that part of these games but even if you pass over to an adult it feels like they have somewhat of a life and great grandkids ensure that you’ll have someone young to pass to too. 

I won’t lie it still has some of the issues of the first game, the cards are still a bit repetitive and there isn’t much incentive for you to play differently to how you usually do but if you enjoy life sims you are somewhat used to this (unfortunately) Ultimately, this is a great game and it’s worth the five stars and DLC!!!
